articles.title: Nomura Prices Largest Single-Bank SASB CMBS in Two Years
articles.narrative: Nomura Securities' commercial real estate lending platform, which launched last summer, has closed its largest sole-bank single-asset, single-borrower (SASB) CMBS deal in nearly two years. The $719 million KELR 2026-MF transaction is backed by a portfolio of 12 multifamily properties and one student housing asset owned by Keller Investment Properties across Utah, Nevada, and Arizona. The floating-rate, interest-only loan has a two-year term with three one-year extension options and refinances existing debt while funding closing costs and reserves. This deal marks Keller Investment Properties' debut in the SASB CMBS market, a significant shift from their historical reliance on agency debt.

data_points.notable_features: Portfolio includes a student housing property serving Utah Valley University.
data_points.project_notes: Keller Investment Properties acquired the portfolio between 2001 and 2022 and has invested $46 million in capital improvements. The CMBS loan refinances $696 million in existing debt and funds $22.2 million in closing-related costs and reserves. The loan has a two-year term with three one-year extension options.

people.name: Larry Kravetz
people.title: Head of U.S. CRE and CMBS

articles.market_intelligence: Multifamily deals continue to be well received by CMBS bond investors. The KELR 2026-MF deal's AAA bonds priced at 135 basis points over the Secured Overnight Financing Rate. The KELR deal's bond classes priced inside of Blackstone's BX Trust 2026-PNDA deal, despite KELR having higher leverage at 77 percent compared to PNDA's 70 percent.

articles.title: No, the Pfizer Near-Disaster Won’t Slow New York’s Conversion Wave
articles.narrative: Despite a structural emergency at the Pfizer building conversion in Midtown, New York City's office-to-residential conversion wave is unlikely to slow. The incident, involving buckling columns at the MetroLoft and David Werner Real Estate Investment project, prompted citywide safety sweeps but is largely considered a 'freak accident' by the industry. While increased scrutiny from lenders and potential new regulations could add to already high construction costs, investor appetite and political will for multifamily housing are expected to sustain the conversion boom. The city's robust conversion market, with 5 million square feet of starts last year and 9.8 million square feet planned, is driven by significant capital investment and the ongoing housing crisis.

data_points.notable_features: 19 stories and 1,600 apartments are being added to the existing structure.
data_points.project_notes: The project experienced a structural emergency in early July involving two buckling columns, leading to temporary supports and a citywide construction safety sweep.

articles.market_intelligence: New York City has the largest conversion market in the country. The city's scaffold law and the 467-m tax exemption (2024) are significant cost pressures for conversion projects.

articles.title: Fashion Nova Expands L.A. Footprint With 133K-SF Warehouse Deal
articles.narrative: Fashion Nova has expanded its logistics operations in Southern California by signing a lease for a 132,888-square-foot warehouse in Santa Fe Springs. This transaction significantly increases the fast-fashion retailer's footprint in the area. The deal reflects a broader trend of increasing leasing momentum in the Los Angeles County industrial market, which has seen a substantial rise in activity and positive net absorption.

data_points.address: 12301 Hawkins Street, Santa Fe Springs, CA
data_points.notable_features: The recently renovated facility includes 12,004 square feet of office space, 30-foot clear heights, 18 dock-high doors, two ground-level doors, and 175 parking spaces.

articles.market_intelligence: Los Angeles County's industrial market saw 15.7 million square feet of leasing activity in Q2, a 40% increase year-over-year, and 2.8 million square feet of positive net absorption, marking its third consecutive positive quarter. Vacancy rates declined to 5% from Q1, while average asking rents dropped 7% year-over-year to $1.19 per square foot per month, and 32.4% from Q2 2023. The Mid-Counties submarket recorded 1.1 million square feet of positive absorption and an average asking rate of $1.23 per square foot.

articles.title: Systima Closes $153M Tax-Exempt CMBS Affordable Housing Deal
articles.narrative: Systima Capital Management closed a $153 million tax-exempt CMBS deal for a portfolio of 1,272 affordable housing units across five states. The transaction, which was significantly oversubscribed by institutional investors, highlights the growing potential for CMBS to finance affordable housing projects. J.P. Morgan served as the lead underwriter, with Wells Fargo as co-manager, demonstrating strong market confidence in the credit protections and demand for affordable housing investments.

data_points.notable_features: Portfolio of properties subsidized by the federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) program, geared toward families earning at or below 60 percent of area median income.
data_points.project_notes: The original loan proceeds were used to fund acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and preservation of the affordable housing communities. Systima retained the subordinate Class B certificates.

articles.financing: Tax-exempt CMBS debt through the Public Finance Authority securitized by a pool of loans on seven properties. Class A-1 certificates rated A-minus and Class A-2 certificates rated BBB-plus by S&P Global Ratings.

articles.title: Todd Rosenberg’s Pebb Capital Buys South Beach Office Building
articles.narrative: Pebb Capital, led by Todd Rosenberg, has acquired the Uno office building in South Beach, Miami, amidst increasing demand from boutique financial firms seeking a presence in the area. The seven-story building, constructed in 2002, offers approximately 100,000 square feet of leasable space and recently underwent renovations, including a 10,000-square-foot expansion by converting a terrace. The transaction was financed with a $69 million loan from Acore Capital, indicating a sale price likely exceeding that amount.

data_points.notable_features: Located in the upscale South of Fifth neighborhood, with 106 covered parking spots.
data_points.project_notes: The seller renovated the interiors during the pandemic and added 10,000 square feet of office space by converting a terrace earlier this month.

articles.market_intelligence: South Beach is experiencing an increase in new Class A office buildings, driven by demand from wealthy executives seeking to work near their homes. The Fifth, a nearby boutique office building, is nearing completion, and another luxury office project, 1100 Fifth Street, is in the pipeline across the street. Ares Management opened a 10,500-square-foot office at the Eighteen Sunset development in Sunset Harbour, completed in 2024.

articles.title: Dwight Capital Provides $66M HUD-Insured Construction Loan for Abilene Multifamily Project
articles.narrative: Dwight Capital has provided a $66 million HUD-insured construction loan for The Lariat at Abilene, a 312-unit multifamily project in West Texas. The garden-style development will feature 13 three-story buildings with a mix of one- and two-bedroom units, along with a clubhouse and various amenities. The financing was originated through HUD's 221(d)(4) program on behalf of Martin Inderman Development.

data_points.notable_features: Garden-style property with a pool, fitness center, pickleball court, and outdoor grilling and dining areas.
data_points.project_notes: Financing originated through HUD's 221(d)(4) program.

articles.title: Marcus & Millichap Negotiates Sale of 165-Unit Self-Storage Facility in Mansfield, Texas
articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap has facilitated the sale of Premium Storage, a 165-unit self-storage facility in Mansfield, Texas. The property was sold by a local owner-operator to a Midwest-based investment group. The facility offers a mix of climate-controlled units and covered and uncovered parking spaces.

data_points.notable_features: Includes 12 climate-controlled units, 107 covered parking spaces, and 46 uncovered parking spaces.

articles.title: Partners Brokers Sale of 14,572 SF Industrial Building in Northwest Houston
articles.narrative: Partners Real Estate has brokered the sale of a 14,572-square-foot industrial building in northwest Houston. The property, originally constructed in 1983, was sold by an undisclosed seller. The buyer and sale price were not disclosed.

articles.title: Island Grill to Open New Restaurant in Houston’s River Oaks Neighborhood
articles.narrative: Island Grill, a Houston-based American Mediterranean restaurant concept, has signed a lease for its sixth location at 2810 Westheimer Road in Houston's River Oaks neighborhood. The new restaurant is anticipated to open in late spring of next year.

articles.title: Jacobson Properties Arranges $13M Sale of Medical Office Building in Liverpool, New York
articles.narrative: Jacobson Properties has facilitated the $13 million sale of a 38,913-square-foot medical office building in Liverpool, New York. The property was fully leased at the time of sale, and the brokerage firm also secured long-term lease extensions with two tenants prior to the transaction. Both the seller and the institutional healthcare real estate investment firm that acquired the asset chose to remain anonymous.

articles.title: Avison Young adds principal, market leader to Houston office
articles.narrative: Avison Young has appointed Matthew Seliger as Principal and Market Leader for its Houston office. In this role, Seliger will spearhead strategic growth initiatives, aiming to expand the firm's service capabilities across brokerage, property management, project management, and valuation, while also focusing on recruiting new talent. His mandate includes growing the Houston platform, strategically expanding the brokerage business, and fostering a collaborative culture for long-term success.

articles.title: Dominium adds VP of property management in Dallas office
articles.narrative: Dominium has appointed Nicole McQuarry as Vice President of Property Management in its Dallas office. In this role, she will be responsible for overseeing all property management operations for Dominium's multifamily portfolio across Texas, focusing on strategic leadership to enhance portfolio performance, operational efficiency, and resident satisfaction. McQuarry brings over 25 years of experience in multifamily housing, having previously managed large residential portfolios and held senior leadership positions focused on operational strategy and asset performance.

articles.title: The NRP Group breaks ground on 336-unit affordable-housing community in Austin area
articles.narrative: The NRP Group has broken ground on Catalina, a 336-unit affordable housing community in Travis County near Austin, Texas. Developed in partnership with the Housing Authority of Travis County (HATC), the project will provide housing for families and professionals earning between 30% and 70% of the Area Median Income. This development marks a significant step in expanding affordable housing options in the region, with initial occupancy expected in September 2027 and full completion by April 2028.

data_points.notable_features: Community offers convenient access to major employment centers including Samsung's semiconductor operations, Tech Ridge, and the EastVillage mixed-use development, with a complimentary shuttle service to local amenities.
data_points.project_notes: The Housing Authority of Travis County contributed $2 million to support deeply affordable homes for households earning no more than 30% AMI. Initial occupancy is slated for September 2027.

articles.title: Associated Bank closes $6.9 million loan to finance industrial building in Pataskala
articles.narrative: Associated Bank has provided a $6.98 million term loan to Transport Properties and GFH Partners for an industrial building in Pataskala, Ohio. The property, completed in 2022, is fully leased and includes significant outdoor parking, aligning with Transport Properties' specialization in industrial outdoor storage.

data_points.notable_features: Includes seven acres of outdoor parking.

people.title: Senior Vice President, Commercial Real Estate

articles.title: Norton Rose Fulbright expands by 20,000 square feet in downtown Houston office building
articles.narrative: Norton Rose Fulbright has expanded its presence at the Norton Rose Fulbright Tower in downtown Houston, adding approximately 20,000 square feet to its existing footprint, bringing its total to 139,000 square feet. This expansion reflects the firm's commitment to client service and talent recruitment, providing enhanced collaborative workspaces and amenities. The building's developer noted that the expansion reinforces the demand for thoughtfully designed, amenity-rich office environments in downtown Houston, with the tower now 63% occupied and over 70% leased.

data_points.notable_features: LEED Platinum, WELL Platinum, and WiredScore Platinum certifications; features hospitality-inspired amenities including a coffee shop, restaurant, fitness facilities, and a rooftop venue called The Summit with landscaped gardens.

people.title: Executive Vice President for Skanska USA Commercial Development in Houston

articles.title: Boston Children’s Hospital sells campus for $62M in leaseback deal
articles.narrative: Boston Children's Hospital has sold its 114,000-square-foot clinical campus in Peabody, MA, to an affiliate of Barings for $62 million in a sale-leaseback transaction. This strategic move provides the hospital with a significant cash infusion and relieves it of debt obligations, while ensuring its continued long-term presence and operations at the North Shore location, where it has been serving the community for three decades.

data_points.notable_features: Clinical campus operating for three decades.
data_points.project_notes: Sale-leaseback transaction.

articles.title: KKR considers offloading real estate lending arm
articles.narrative: KKR Real Estate Finance Trust (KREF) is exploring strategic alternatives, including a potential sale of the company or disposition of assets, following a challenging second quarter. The real estate lending arm of KKR reported a $121.8 million loss on its $4.5 billion loan portfolio, which has decreased from $5.1 billion in the first quarter. Despite resolving two watchlist loans and repurchasing shares, KREF is still managing six watchlisted properties, including office and life sciences assets, as it continues its "year of transition."

articles.title: Housing Notes: The Great Wealth Transfer is going to be underwhelming
articles.narrative: This article argues that the anticipated "Great Wealth Transfer" from Baby Boomers to their heirs will be underwhelming and will likely exacerbate the wealth gap rather than enrich the middle class. The author supports this by citing data indicating that only a small percentage of Americans receive substantial inheritances, with the vast majority receiving little to none. The piece also discusses the long-term trend of increasing unit sizes in Manhattan's co-op and condo market, driven by rising land values and developer economics, and links this to declining birth rates which may soften demand for larger homes in the future.

articles.title: NYC’s top deals: Witkoff, Access Industries sell One High Line unit for $14M
articles.narrative: Enbergar NY LLC sold an office building at 122 East 55th Street in Midtown for $7.7 million to 122 East 55th Street LLC. Additionally, a mixed-use residential and commercial property at 236 Broadway in Williamsburg was sold by 236 Broadway Equities LLC to 236 Broadway Realty LLC for $6.4 million. These transactions represent two of the top commercial deals recorded in New York City on July 23.

data_points.address: 122 East 55th Street, New York City, NY

articles.title: COGE greenlights permit, city contract ballot questions
articles.narrative: New York City voters will consider five proposed charter amendments in November, aimed at reforming the city's permitting and procurement systems. Key proposals include establishing a centralized hub for construction permits, streamlining the waterfront permitting process under the Department of Buildings, and expediting the city's procurement of goods and services. The measures also seek to give the city more flexibility in repurposing small public lots and acquiring office space, as well as setting a reserves target for the city's rainy day fund and simplifying outdoor dining applications. The Commission on Government Efficiency (COGE) unanimously approved these recommendations, with the goal of making New York more affordable and efficient.

articles.title: Kings Capital buys vacant FiDi Building, plans for conversion
articles.narrative: Kings Capital has acquired a 17-story vacant building at 69 Gold Street in Manhattan's Financial District from New York Presbyterian Hospital for $30.1 million. The development group plans to convert the former 90-unit staff housing into 108 market-rate residential units with ground-floor retail. The total project cost is estimated at $60 million, with a $41 million construction loan from Derby Copeland reportedly nearing completion. The building, vacant for nearly a decade, will undergo a full rehabilitation, including a new rooftop space.

data_points.address: 69 Gold Street, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: 17-story building with planned rooftop space offering views of the East River and Brooklyn Bridge.
data_points.project_notes: Building was previously 90 units of staff housing for New York Presbyterian Hospital and has been vacant for nearly a decade. Units have been gutted, allowing for a full rehabilitation. The developer will not rely on tax exemptions like the 485x program.

articles.title: SL Green cashes in on Manhattan office rebound
articles.narrative: SL Green Realty Corp. has significantly raised its full-year earnings guidance, driven by robust Manhattan office leasing activity, particularly in Midtown's Class A market. The company's CEO, Marc Holliday, noted a growing scarcity of premier space due to limited new construction and conversions of older buildings to residential use, which has created a landlord-favorable environment. Strong demand from financial services and AI-driven tech companies, exemplified by a 100,000-square-foot lease at 11 Madison Avenue, has contributed to substantial rent growth across SL Green's portfolio.
articles.market_intelligence: Midtown's Class A office space supply is tightening due to a dearth of new construction and conversions of older office buildings to apartments. Asking rents have been rising throughout the year, with strong leasing spreads anticipated. The financial services sector is performing exceptionally well, contributing to an "extraordinary, prolonged surge in business activity" in the city. AI-driven tech leasing is also a significant driver of demand.

articles.title: Pfizer building incident pits banner project with a conversion pitfall
articles.narrative: A partial stop-work order at MetroLoft Management's conversion of the former Pfizer headquarters in Midtown East is complicating the project's future, as interest continues to accrue on its $720 million construction loan. The incident, involving buckled columns, highlights the inherent challenges and financial risks associated with office-to-residential conversions, particularly the impact of construction delays on project budgets and timelines. Despite the developer's optimism for a swift restart, the need to reconstruct 15 floors is expected to significantly increase costs and extend the timeline for this ambitious 1,600-unit luxury residential conversion.

data_points.address: 235 East 42nd Street, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Conversion of two existing buildings (33-story and 10-story) into a single luxury residential tower, with plans to add four floors to the taller building and 19 stories to the smaller building.
data_points.project_notes: The project is converting the former Pfizer headquarters, which served as the pharmaceutical giant's headquarters for 62 years. The property consists of two buildings: a 33-story structure at 235 East 42nd Street and a 10-story structure at 219 East 42nd Street. The developer plans to reconstruct 15 floors after two columns were found buckled on the 21st floor.

articles.market_intelligence: Office-to-residential conversion loans are highly project-specific, with pricing influenced by factors such as the amount of structural work required and building occupancy. The former Pfizer headquarters was vacant, which typically reduces risk and expense, but extensive structural work likely offset some of that benefit. The loan for this project is speculated to have an interest rate of approximately 650 basis points over SOFR, or about 10 percent, though a debt broker suggested it might be lower due to the building's vacancy.

articles.title: Forest Development, Kast Construction face off in legal battle over Lake Park condo
articles.narrative: Forest Development and Kast Construction are engaged in a legal dispute over the Nautilus 220 condominium project in Lake Park, Florida. Forest Development, the developer, initiated a lawsuit alleging incomplete work, improper supervision by Kast Construction leading to water damage and delays, and a refusal to release liens on sold properties. Kast Construction, the builder, countersued, claiming Forest Development failed to make $11.4 million in progress payments and submitted late and inaccurate change orders that disrupted the project. The legal battle highlights significant financial disagreements and project management issues between the developer and the general contractor.

data_points.address: 220 Lake Shore Dr, Lake Park, FL
data_points.notable_features: Two-tower, 24-story complex with residential, retail, office, and restaurant space.
data_points.project_notes: Kast Construction placed an $11.4 million lien on the project last month. Various subcontractors have filed $2.9 million in liens.

articles.title: American Landmark expands South Florida apartment portfolio with Palm Beach County acquisition
articles.narrative: American Landmark Apartments has expanded its South Florida multifamily portfolio with the acquisition of Savona Grand, a 214-unit apartment community located between Boynton Beach and Lake Worth Beach in Palm Beach County. The Tampa-based investment manager plans to invest in upgrades at the property, which was previously sold in 2019 for $47.8 million. The acquisition brings American Landmark's South Florida portfolio to four properties, reflecting the company's strategy to capitalize on Palm Beach County's strong resident and employer growth amidst constrained new supply.

data_points.address: 7132 Colony Club Drive, Palm Beach County, FL
data_points.notable_features: Amenities include a pool, fitness center, clubhouse, basketball and tennis courts, pickleball court, dog park, and gated entry. The property is near Florida’s Turnpike, Interstate 95, HCA Florida JFK Hospital, and Palm Beach State College.
data_points.project_notes: The property was previously acquired by Southstar Capital Group in 2019 for $47.8 million, with a $32 million mortgage from Hunt Mortgage Capital.

articles.title: Pebb buys office building for over $70M as Miami Beach strives to shed party-town image
articles.narrative: Pebb Capital has acquired the Uno South Pointe office building in Miami Beach for over $70 million, signaling continued investor confidence in South Beach's emergence as a serious office market. The seven-story, nearly 97,500-square-foot building, which was renovated last year and is planning a penthouse addition, is approximately 97 percent leased. The transaction underscores a broader effort by market stakeholders and officials to transform the area from a party destination into a vibrant office hub.

data_points.notable_features: Seven-story building with over 10,000 square feet of outdoor terraces, renovated last year, and a 10,100-square-foot penthouse addition planned for early next year.
data_points.project_notes: The building was originally named The Atlantic Center. The seller's identity was hidden for years through entity Yantra 119.

articles.title: Ken Griffin wins city approval to buy historic cottage near Citadel’s HQ for $3M
articles.narrative: Ken Griffin has received city approval to purchase a historic cottage in Miami for $2.98 million, located near Citadel's future headquarters in Brickell. The 121-year-old Dr. James M. Jackson Medical Office, currently home to Dade Heritage Trust, will be relocated to Coconut Grove, with Griffin funding the move and preservation. This transaction is part of Griffin's broader development strategy in Brickell, where he is assembling land for a new 54-story office tower for Citadel and Citadel Securities, along with a 300-unit apartment building and parking garage.

data_points.property_name: Dr. James M. Jackson Medical Office
data_points.notable_features: Historic cottage, former office and surgical center of Miami's first resident physician.
data_points.project_notes: The property will be relocated to Coconut Grove, with funding for relocation and preservation provided by the buyer. The buyer previously acquired a 2.5-acre site for $363 million in 2022 for the main headquarters development.

articles.title: Mandarin Oriental Brickell Key, Live Local high-rise among $420M-plus South Florida construction permits for week ending July 22, 2026
articles.narrative: South Florida saw over $420 million in construction permits issued for the week ending July 22, 2026, highlighted by a $240 million permit for The Residences at Mandarin Oriental, Miami and Mandarin Oriental Hotel on Brickell Key. This redevelopment by Swire Properties will feature condos and a hotel across 1.35 million square feet, replacing the previously demolished hotel towers. Other significant permits included a $95 million mixed-use project by HA Emprendimientos, a $21.3 million mixed-use development by Lore Development Group and Element Development, and a $19 million municipal office building for the City of Miami Administration Building.

articles.title: “It’s out of control”: Inside Chicago’s bidding war summer
articles.narrative: Chicago's residential real estate market is experiencing an unusually hot summer, characterized by competitive bidding wars and rising prices, driven by scarce inventory. The Illinois median home price reached $345,000 in June, a 6.2% annual increase, while Chicago's city-specific median home price surpassed $400,000 in March and has remained above that mark. Brokers note that demand, particularly in neighborhoods like Lincoln Park, is "out of control," leading to homes selling quickly and often above asking price. This trend suggests that the typical post-July 4th slowdown may be shorter than usual, with expectations for continued price growth if interest rates remain below 7%.

articles.title: Little-known foreign entity and lender locked in $25M foreclosure of O’Hare hotels
articles.narrative: A dual-branded hotel near O'Hare International Airport is facing foreclosure after its developer allegedly failed to repay a $25 million construction mortgage that matured in 2022. The unpaid balance on the note currently stands at $23 million. The lender has also requested the appointment of a receiver for the property, which was repurposed from an existing building into the Hyatt La Quinta hotel using the 2014 loan.

data_points.project_notes: The property is also encumbered by a $7 million mortgage taken out in 2023 from International Bank. The original construction loan was tied to the U.S. EB-5 visa program.

articles.title: $27M Lakeview co-op building renovation tops Chicago’s construction permits: Week ending July 23, 2026
articles.narrative: The largest construction permit issued in Chicago last week was for a $27 million infrastructure renovation at a co-op building in Lakeview. The project at 655 West Irving Park Road involves replacing water risers, waste and vent piping, and HVAC piping, along with installing new ceilings on three floors. Other significant permits included a $23.2 million interior renovation for an apartment building in Auburn Gresham, a $17.5 million restroom alteration project at O'Hare International Airport, and a $15 million new residential building in the West Loop.

data_points.address: 655 West Irving Park Road, Chicago, IL
data_points.notable_features: Infrastructure renovation including water risers, waste and vent piping, HVAC piping replacement, and new ceilings on three floors.

articles.title: Former Blackhawk Adrian Aucoin lists Hinsdale home for $6 million
articles.narrative: Former Chicago Blackhawks defenseman Adrian Aucoin has listed his 6,459-square-foot personal residence in Hinsdale, IL, for $5.7 million. The seven-bedroom, eight-bathroom home, designed by Michael Abraham and built in 2017, features a chef's kitchen and a heated chlorine pool. The listing reflects the highly competitive Hinsdale market, where homes are selling quickly due to strong buyer demand and limited inventory.

data_points.notable_features: Designed by Michael Abraham, features a chef's kitchen and a heated chlorine pool.

articles.title: UrbanStreet targets former Motorola office for residential conversion
articles.narrative: UrbanStreet Group is planning a residential conversion of a former Motorola office building in Schaumburg, IL, as part of its larger District at Veridian development. The project involves transforming the existing 360,200-square-foot building and constructing a new four-story sister building, creating approximately 300 residential units. This redevelopment is a key component of the $1 billion mixed-use megadevelopment, which aims to establish a walkable, urban-style downtown in the suburban area.

data_points.notable_features: Residential conversion of a six-story atrium office building, with an additional four-story sister building planned.
data_points.project_notes: The 225-acre site was previously acquired by UrbanStreet Group a decade ago. The overall development aims to create a walkable, 'mini-urban' downtown element in Schaumburg.

articles.title: Viceroy signs onto Austin’s new $235M luxury condo project with branding rights
articles.narrative: Pearlstone Partners has secured Viceroy Residences to brand its 146-unit luxury condominium project in Austin, marking the city's first branded condo complex not attached to a hotel. The $235 million development, which broke ground in March 2025, will offer a range of wellness-focused amenities. The project aims to attract buyers seeking larger, high-end units in a walkable downtown-adjacent location, with sales expected to launch in September.

data_points.notable_features: Austin's first branded condo complex unattached to a hotel, offering wellness amenities including a 75-foot pool, spa, and fitness center.
data_points.project_notes: Previously named The Belvedere. Phase two will add 40-50 additional units; no timeline yet for this phase. Units range from 760 to 4,200 SF and are priced from $800,000 to $6 million.

articles.title: 500 acres in Spicewood surrounded by luxury homes hit market with $44M price tag
articles.narrative: A 517-acre parcel known as Flying X Ranch in Spicewood, west of Austin, has been listed for sale with an asking price of $44 million, or $85,000 per acre. The majority owner, Calvin Chen, is seeking a buyer interested in developing a unique, culture-focused experience, rather than traditional industrial or automotive uses. The property is situated in an area experiencing significant luxury development, near the Colorado River and Pedernales Falls State Park.

data_points.notable_features: Surrounded by luxury homes, close to Colorado River and Pedernales Falls State Park.
data_points.project_notes: Owner is seeking a buyer interested in 'culture' and unique experiences, rejecting offers from industrial companies, an aviation company, and a car manufacturer.

articles.title: Jerry Jones sells 17 Cowboys Way to Hobbs Brook
articles.narrative: Jerry Jones' real estate firm has sold an 11-story, 300,000-square-foot office building at 17 Cowboys Way in Frisco, TX, to Massachusetts-based Hobbs Brook Real Estate. The property is part of The Star, a mixed-use campus that serves as the Dallas Cowboys' corporate headquarters. This acquisition marks Hobbs Brook's entry into the Texas real estate market. The building is 98% leased, though one of its tenants recently announced layoffs.

data_points.notable_features: First multi-tenant office facility built in The Star since the Cowboys headquarters opened in 2016.

articles.market_intelligence: The Star is a 91-acre, $2 billion mixed-use campus. The Mix, a 112-acre, $3 billion development, is two miles away. FC Dallas is spending $182 million to overhaul Toyota Stadium.

articles.title: Invesco takes $100M-plus hit on sale of Houston’s Williams Tower
articles.narrative: Williams Companies has acquired the 64-story Williams Tower in Houston, TX, for $300 million from Invesco Real Estate. The transaction, which includes a parking garage, represents a significant loss for Invesco, which purchased the property in 2013 for $412 million. The energy company, which previously occupied space in the tower, aims to accommodate future growth in the Houston market through this purchase. The tower, completed in 1983, maintains an 83 percent occupancy rate, with several major tenants expanding or relocating their headquarters there recently.

data_points.notable_features: 64-story office tower located near the Galleria, includes a parking garage.
data_points.project_notes: Previously known as Transco Tower, developed by Hines. Williams Companies acquired Transco in 1995 and formally changed the tower's name the same year. Invesco purchased the property in 2013 for $412 million.

articles.market_intelligence: The Galleria submarket recorded 200,000 square feet of positive absorption in 2025. While prestigious, highly-amenitized towers in Houston's downtown areas are performing well, other office properties are struggling, with some facing demolition or being purchased by large tenants at lower values.

articles.title: SF office market continues recovery with another AI-powered lease in South Beach
articles.narrative: Fintech firm Brex, recently acquired by Capital One, has significantly expanded its San Francisco footprint by signing a full-building, 200,000-square-foot lease at 270 Brannan Street in the South Beach neighborhood. This move more than triples the company's previous office space and reflects a growing trend of AI-backed firms driving office demand and positive net absorption in the city. The company's president noted the momentum around AI as a key factor in their decision to commit to a larger physical presence in San Francisco.

data_points.notable_features: Located in the South Beach neighborhood, near OpenAI's headquarters. The building is Class A.
data_points.project_notes: Brex previously leased approximately 100,000 square feet in the same building last year after returning to San Francisco.

articles.market_intelligence: San Francisco experienced its seventh consecutive quarter of positive net absorption in Q2 2026. AI startups accounted for approximately one-third of all leasing activity in the city, totaling nearly 1 million square feet out of 3 million square feet of overall leasing activity. Mission Bay had the lowest office vacancy at 17%, while Yerba Buena had the highest at 62.7%. Class A buildings comprised 77% of leasing activity in Q2 2026.

articles.title: Google recommits to Sunnyvale’s tightening office market in 2M sf lease renewal
articles.narrative: Google has renewed its lease for 2.1 million square feet across five buildings at Moffett Place and two buildings at Moffett Gateway in Sunnyvale, reaffirming its commitment to the Silicon Valley office market. This significant renewal signals a shift from the company's previous space-cutting strategy and contributes to reducing the substantial office availability in the region. The properties, developed by Jay Paul Company, are a key part of Silicon Valley's office landscape.

data_points.address: 151 to 1195 Borregas Avenue / 1225 Crossman Avenue, Sunnyvale, CA
data_points.notable_features: Moffett Place is the second-largest office complex in Silicon Valley.
data_points.project_notes: Jay Paul Company developed Moffett Place and Moffett Gateway in 2016. Google previously exited offices at 237 Moffett Park Drive, moving Google Cloud operations to 100 and 200 West Caribbean Drive.

articles.market_intelligence: Overall office availability in Silicon Valley is 18.2 percent, with Class A availability in Sunnyvale at 10.9 percent. Amazon recently leased 320,000 square feet in Sunnyvale. Apple acquired over $1 billion in offices in Sunnyvale and Cupertino last year, including a $162 million purchase at 684 West Maude Avenue last month. Fortinet bought two commercial buildings at 140 and 144 Commercial Street for $15 million last month, adding to a $47 million purchase of seven properties earlier this year.

articles.narrative: Shorenstein has acquired a six-story, 76,700-square-foot office building at 550 Allerton Street in Redwood City for $78 million, or $1,018 per square foot. The property, developed in 2018 by Premia Capital, is 81 percent leased with a venture capital law firm as its anchor tenant. This transaction reflects a premium price for the Redwood City market, indicating strong demand for high-quality downtown office assets in the Peninsula and Silicon Valley.

articles.title: Former Charles Schwab CEO sells SF condo after 10 years. How did he only make $18K?
articles.narrative: The former CEO of Charles Schwab, David Pottruck, sold his three-bedroom, three-bathroom condo in San Francisco's Rincon Hill neighborhood for just under $6.7 million, realizing a modest profit of $18,300 after a decade of ownership. The transaction highlights the divergent trends in San Francisco's luxury housing market, where single-family homes are experiencing significant gains driven by the AI boom, while even high-end condominiums like those in the Lumina towers have struggled to appreciate, with many selling at or below their 2016 prices. The buyer, Ledion Bitincka, is the chief technology officer at an AI data firm, reflecting the new wave of wealth entering the market.

data_points.notable_features: Located on the 26th floor of a sleek, 656-unit luxury condominium complex.
data_points.project_notes: Seller purchased the condo in 2016 for just under $6.7 million.

articles.market_intelligence: San Francisco's luxury housing market shows a divergence between single-family homes, which are seeing increased demand and appreciation due to the AI boom, and luxury condominiums, which have not experienced similar gains. Median condo sales prices per square foot in San Francisco peaked at $1,200 in 2020, dropped to $950 in 2025, and saw a slight increase to $990 in early 2026, marking the first real boost since the pandemic. Over 75% of condos sold in the Lumina towers since last year went for at or below their 2016 prices.

articles.title: Inflation Could Stay Higher: What it Means for CRE
articles.narrative: This article analyzes the potential for sustained inflation and its implications for commercial real estate, despite a recent dip in the Consumer Price Index. The author argues that ongoing geopolitical tensions and persistent inflation in key sectors like energy, food, housing, and medical care suggest that elevated prices may continue, potentially leading to further federal interest rate hikes. However, the author concludes that commercial real estate remains a resilient investment, with the risk of rate increases largely priced into current lending rates, and all major property types demonstrating positive space demand and stable fundamentals.

articles.title: Office’s New Purpose: Affiliation
articles.narrative: A new report from CBRE indicates that global office utilization saw its largest annual gain in four years in 2025, rising to 53% from 38% the previous year. The report, "Global Workplace & Occupancy Insights," highlights that organizations designing their office spaces for collaboration, culture, and connection are experiencing the strongest attendance gains. The primary purpose of the office has shifted from individual workspaces to fostering interaction, with 93% of respondents citing colleague collaboration as a main reason for coming in. Consequently, space dedicated to individual workstations decreased from 56% to 35% between 2021 and 2025, while collaborative areas expanded from 12% to 56%. The report suggests that office performance is now measured by what the workplace enables, rather than just its occupancy rate, and that quality environments and hybrid coordination are more effective than mandates for encouraging attendance.

articles.title: How AI Is Transforming Utility Real Estate and Workplace Portfolios
articles.narrative: A JLL report highlights how artificial intelligence is transforming utility companies' real estate and workplace portfolios beyond just grid management. By centralizing facility and asset data, AI can identify inefficiencies, recommend improvements, and enable predictive maintenance, leading to significant cost savings and enhanced sustainability. The technology also aids in strategic real estate planning by analyzing lease data and occupancy trends, allowing utilities to optimize office space utilization and reduce operational expenses, particularly for costs not recoverable through utility rates.

articles.title: Beyond the Flight to Quality: The Office Questions That Aren’t Being Asked
articles.narrative: This article compiles insights from various commercial real estate leaders, moving beyond common discussions of remote work and interest rates to explore deeper, unasked questions shaping the office market. Experts from brokerage, investment, debt placement, and research weigh in on topics ranging from the impact of AI on building readiness and corporate geographic footprints to the importance of workplace friendships and neighborhood amenities. The consensus suggests a need for a more nuanced evaluation of office assets, considering factors like Class B potential, the alignment of financing structures with lender expectations, and the long-term rental upside for top-tier properties.

articles.title: M&T RCC Provides $141M Bridge Loan to Newly Built Turtle Bay Apartments
articles.narrative: M&T Realty Capital Corporation provided a $141.4 million bridge loan to an ownership group led by Global Holdings, MAG Partners, and Safanad for Anagram Turtle Bay, a newly constructed 194-unit multifamily community in Manhattan's Turtle Bay neighborhood. The three-year loan refinances the property's construction financing and is intended to support the asset through its final lease-up and stabilization phase before securing long-term permanent financing. This bridge financing strategy is crucial for high-quality multifamily assets nearing stabilization in the current market, offering flexibility and execution certainty during the transition.

articles.title: The World Cup Filled Stadiums. Hotel Rooms Were A Different Story
articles.narrative: The 2026 World Cup, while setting attendance records, did not fully meet the hospitality industry's expectations for a hotel bonanza. Hotels saw strong revenue per available room (RevPAR) growth and average daily rate (ADR) increases on match days, particularly around marquee games. However, this was offset by fans booking last-minute, staying for shorter durations than projected, and a significant drop in convention and business travel in host cities, which largely displaced traditional demand. Performance varied widely by market, with some cities experiencing substantial gains while others saw overall occupancy dip below normal summer levels.

articles.title: Former Arms Dealer Launches Takeover Of Heartland Apartment Portfolio
articles.narrative: A legal battle has erupted over Vesta Capital, a multifamily firm, involving its founder Marc Kulick, his former business partners, and lender Efraim Diveroli. Kulick defaulted on high-interest loans from Diveroli's YSA Investments, leading to Diveroli's team taking over management of 10 properties in Tulsa, Oklahoma, and initiating foreclosure proceedings on at least nine properties. Kulick's former partners allege he committed fraud to fund a lavish lifestyle, while Kulick claims he is a victim of a hostile takeover and is fighting to regain control of over 30 assets. Fannie Mae has also initiated foreclosure proceedings on eight properties within the portfolio, and several holding companies under Vesta's structure have filed for bankruptcy.

data_points.project_notes: The portfolio includes approximately 35 owned or managed properties across Oklahoma, Kansas, and Arkansas. The legal disputes stem from an unexpected 43-44% increase in master insurance policy costs from 2023 to 2024, which led Kulick to seek alternative financing from Efraim Diveroli's family office. Loans taken between October 2024 and July 2025 included a 7,000% interest rate that compounded daily. YSA Investments took over daily operations at Vesta's Tulsa properties on July 20, 2026, after Kulick defaulted on the debt.

articles.title: Why Google's $205B AI Spending Plan Sparked Wall Street Turmoil
articles.narrative: Google's parent company, Alphabet, reported strong second-quarter earnings with cloud segment revenue growing 82% year-over-year to $24.8B and top-line revenue up 24%. However, the company's announcement of a significant increase in its estimated capital expenditures for 2026 to $205B, primarily for data centers and AI infrastructure, has caused Wall Street turmoil. This escalated spending, which is expected to continue into 2027, means Google is currently spending more than it generates, leading to negative free cash flow. Analysts suggest that while the market is generally anxious about the tech sector's AI infrastructure spending, Google's stock plunge may specifically indicate concerns that the company is falling behind in the AI arms race, with its investments not yet translating into a clear competitive advantage.

articles.title: Prologis To Buy Segro In One Of Industrial's Largest Mergers Ever
articles.narrative: Prologis has made a firm final preliminary offer to acquire UK-based industrial developer Segro for over $18.7 billion, a $500 million increase from its previous rejected offer. Segro's board has indicated it would recommend this offer to shareholders if officially made. This potential deal, one of the largest industrial REIT mergers ever, would add 117 million square feet of European industrial and data center space valued at $29.3 billion to Prologis' portfolio. The acquisition is expected to accelerate Prologis' growth strategy, particularly in the data center sector.

data_points.notable_features: Includes European industrial and data center space.
data_points.project_notes: Segro's board unanimously rejected three previous offers from Prologis. The offer includes a partial cash alternative of up to $4.6 billion. The deadline for Prologis' formal offer has been extended to August 12.

articles.title: Pennsylvania Data Center Boom Skips The Lehigh Valley
articles.narrative: The Lehigh Valley, despite its robust power infrastructure inherited from a manufacturing past, is not emerging as a significant hub for data center development. This is primarily due to a scarcity of available development sites, elevated land valuations, and increasing community opposition during the entitlement process. While some smaller warehouse-to-data center conversions are occurring, the region's industrial market is instead attracting manufacturing-oriented tenants requiring substantial power for producing components that support data centers elsewhere.
